primitives.name: DiContainer
primitives.purpose: Registry that resolves a typed request for a dependency into a constructed instance obeying the declared lifetime scope.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Callable, Protocol, Type, TypeVar

T = TypeVar('T')

class DiContainer(Protocol):
    def register(self, iface: Type[T], impl: Type[T] | Callable[..., T], *, scope: str) -> None: ...
    def resolve(self, iface: Type[T]) -> T: ...
    def create_scope(self) -> 'DiContainer': ...
invariants: MUST resolve a dependency graph without re-entering a partially-constructed node (cycle detection SHALL raise).
NEVER returns an instance whose declared scope outlives the resolving scope (scoped CANNOT leak into singleton).
ALWAYS disposes instances it owns when the owning scope ends; callers MUST NOT dispose externally-created instances.
MUST NOT silently replace a prior registration for the same key; re-registration SHALL be explicit.
register() MUST accept the interface type as the resolution key; keyed registrations MUST use an extra discriminator.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream code registers services via register() or a provider decorator; to plug a non-default container, implement the Protocol and bind an adapter that forwards resolve()/register()/create_scope() without changing lifetime semantics.
primitives.consumption_example:
def build_container(c: DiContainer) -> None:
    c.register(UserRepo, SqlUserRepo, scope='singleton')
    c.register(RequestClock, SystemClock, scope='scoped')

def handle(container: DiContainer) -> None:
    with container.create_scope() as scope:
        repo = scope.resolve(UserRepo)
        repo.save(...)

sources.source: Quarkus 3.x Guide — Contexts and Dependency Injection

primitives.why_essential: Without a shared container contract, every tool grows its own construction code; cross-tool substitution (fakes in tests, adapters in prod) CANNOT work and lifetime bugs become per-feature surprises.
alternatives_considered: Hand-wired constructors per entry point — loses uniform test substitution
Service-locator singleton — hides dependencies and defeats unit tests
Module import side-effects — couples wiring to import order

primitives.name: LifetimeScope
primitives.purpose: Typed enumeration that fixes how long a resolved instance lives: the whole process, one request, or one injection point.
primitives.api_signature:
from enum import Enum

class LifetimeScope(str, Enum):
    SINGLETON = 'singleton'
    SCOPED = 'scoped'
    TRANSIENT = 'transient'
invariants: SINGLETON instances MUST be shared process-wide and created at most once per container.
SCOPED instances MUST be created at most once per scope and disposed when the scope ends.
TRANSIENT instances MUST be created per resolution call and NEVER reused across call sites.
A SINGLETON MUST NEVER depend on a SCOPED or TRANSIENT disposable that requires a live request scope.
The value set MUST be closed: any new lifetime requires an explicit enum addition, NEVER a string literal.
primitives.extension_contract: Alternative frameworks map their native lifetimes (Spring 'request', Nest.js 'REQUEST', ASP.NET 'Scoped', Quarkus '@RequestScoped') onto this enum via an adapter that translates register() calls; new lifetimes require extending the enum, not bypassing it.
primitives.consumption_example:
def register_scoped(c: DiContainer, iface: type, impl: type) -> None:
    scope = LifetimeScope.SCOPED
    c.register(iface, impl, scope=scope.value)

assert LifetimeScope.SINGLETON.value == 'singleton'
primitives.why_essential: Mixing lifetimes is the #1 source of latent bugs: a shared singleton holding a scoped dependency crashes only under load. One vocabulary SHALL be enforceable at registration time rather than debugged in production.
alternatives_considered: Free-form string scope names — no compile-time check, drift across tools
Boolean 'shared/not shared' — collapses SCOPED and SINGLETON distinction
Framework-specific annotations only — breaks cross-framework portability

primitives.name: RequestContext
primitives.purpose: Per-request bag that carries identity, headers, correlation id, and free-form assigns through the handler stack without global state.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Any, Mapping, Protocol

class RequestContext(Protocol):
    request_id: str
    principal: object | None
    headers: Mapping[str, str]
    assigns: dict[str, Any]

    def put(self, key: str, value: Any) -> 'RequestContext': ...
    def halt(self) -> 'RequestContext': ...
invariants: MUST be constructed once per inbound request and disposed when the response is sent.
NEVER leaks across request boundaries; a background task CANNOT reuse a parent context as live state.
put() MUST be idempotent for the same (key, value); overwriting an existing key SHALL be explicit.
halt() MUST cause subsequent middleware/interceptors to skip, but SHALL NOT abort already-queued response bytes.
request_id MUST be populated before the first user code runs; a missing id SHALL be replaced with a generated UUID.
primitives.extension_contract: Middleware reads/writes via put() and assigns; cross-cutting concerns subscribe by registering a plug/interceptor/middleware component that receives the context, mutates assigns, and returns the context (or halts).
primitives.why_essential: Any feature touching identity, tenancy, or tracing needs the same per-request state surface; if every tool defines its own, observability and authorization fragment and memory leaks appear at shutdown.
alternatives_considered: Thread-local globals — break under asyncio/threadpools
Per-call argument threading — explodes function signatures across layers
Pass dict everywhere — no type safety, no lifecycle guarantees

primitives.name: CurrentPrincipal
primitives.purpose: Read-only view of the authenticated identity for the active request, including subject id, tenant, roles, and claim set.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import FrozenSet, Mapping

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CurrentPrincipal:
    subject_id: str
    tenant_id: str | None
    roles: FrozenSet[str]
    claims: Mapping[str, str]
    is_anonymous: bool
invariants: MUST be immutable once bound to a RequestContext; a later middleware CANNOT mutate subject_id.
NEVER represents a successful auth state with is_anonymous=True; these two fields SHALL be mutually exclusive.
roles MUST be a frozen set; consumers CANNOT add a role at call time to bypass authorization.
subject_id MUST be stable across requests for the same identity; rotation NEVER happens silently.
Serialization for logs MUST omit raw claims by default; sensitive claim values SHALL be redacted.
primitives.extension_contract: An auth middleware/plug/guard decodes the incoming credential and binds a CurrentPrincipal to the RequestContext; downstream code reads it via dependency injection or context.principal and CANNOT construct one without passing through the registered provider.
primitives.why_essential: Identity threads through almost every business rule; if each tool invents its own 'current user' type, authorization logic duplicates and drifts and audit trails stop agreeing on who did what.
alternatives_considered: Pass a raw JWT string everywhere — forces repeated parsing and errors
Put user dict into RequestContext.assigns — loses type discipline
Module-level globals like Rails pre-7 — unsafe under threaded/async models

primitives.name: CorrelationId
primitives.purpose: Opaque string that travels with a request across services and log lines so a reader can stitch together the work done for one user action.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import NewType, Protocol

CorrelationId = NewType('CorrelationId', str)

class CorrelationIdProvider(Protocol):
    def current(self) -> CorrelationId: ...
    def generate(self) -> CorrelationId: ...
invariants: MUST be populated for every inbound request before the first log line is emitted.
NEVER regenerates a present upstream id (propagates 'traceparent'/'X-Request-Id' when valid).
Generated ids MUST use a cryptographically-random 16+ byte encoding; sequential counters SHALL NOT be used.
MUST appear in every emitted log, metric exemplar, and outbound HTTP request header.
CANNOT be mutated mid-request; a new id SHALL mean a new logical request.
primitives.extension_contract: A middleware/plug/interceptor reads the inbound header, or generates via the provider, then binds the id to the RequestContext and the logger MDC; structured-log formatters subscribe via a filter or hook to inject it automatically.

sources.source: Ruby on Rails 7 — CurrentAttributes request_id example

primitives.why_essential: Distributed debugging CANNOT work if each tool picks its own id format and header name; a single contract lets logs, metrics, and traces be joined without a specialist's knowledge.
alternatives_considered: Only OpenTelemetry trace-id — omits requests outside the tracer
Per-service random ids — breaks cross-hop correlation
Autoincrementing request counter — leaks traffic volume, collides across nodes

primitives.name: MiddlewarePipeline
primitives.purpose: Ordered chain of components that each transform the RequestContext and decide whether to call the next, enabling cross-cutting concerns.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Awaitable, Callable, Protocol

Next = Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]

class Middleware(Protocol):
    async def __call__(self, ctx: RequestContext, call_next: Next) -> None: ...

class MiddlewarePipeline(Protocol):
    def use(self, mw: Middleware) -> 'MiddlewarePipeline': ...
    async def run(self, ctx: RequestContext) -> None: ...
invariants: Execution order MUST be the registration order; swap or insert operations SHALL be explicit, never implicit.
A middleware that does NOT await call_next MUST short-circuit the remainder of the pipeline.
Each middleware CANNOT bypass downstream error handling: exceptions NEVER skip registered error filters.
Registration MUST be frozen before run() is first called; adding middleware at request time SHALL raise.
MUST produce a response even if every middleware halts; an unhandled halt SHALL yield a 500 by contract.
primitives.extension_contract: Consumers add behavior by implementing Middleware and calling pipeline.use(); alternative styles (NestJS interceptor, Plug module, ASP.NET IMiddleware, Rack app) MUST be bound via an adapter that forwards (ctx, call_next) and preserves ordering.
primitives.why_essential: Authentication, logging, rate limiting, and error shaping are the same kind of component; without one chain contract, each feature reimplements ordering and every new concern reopens the same debate.
alternatives_considered: AOP via bytecode weaving — invisible and hard to debug
Decorators per handler — combinatorial explosion
Monkey-patching dispatcher — breaks framework upgrades

primitives.name: RequestGuard
primitives.purpose: Predicate invoked before a handler runs that returns allow/deny based on RequestContext and CurrentPrincipal, short-circuiting the pipeline on deny.
invariants: A False return MUST prevent the handler from running and SHALL produce a 401/403 response.
Guards MUST NOT mutate the request body; they CANNOT transform payloads, only accept or reject.
Multiple guards MUST be composed with logical AND: any False blocks the request.
Guards MUST execute before interceptors/pipes but after authentication middleware has bound a principal.
A guard that raises NEVER gets silently treated as allow; exceptions SHALL map to 500 by the error filter.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream tools implement RequestGuard and register via a decorator (e.g. @UseGuards on a controller, a register() call on the pipeline, or a Plug inserted before dispatch); guards compose, they CANNOT replace one another.

sources.locator: docs.nestjs.com/guards — canActivate(context) returns boolean | Promise | Observable

primitives.why_essential: Authorization must be declarative and uniform across handlers; when each handler reimplements role checks, audit coverage CANNOT be proven and policy changes SHALL ripple unsafely.
alternatives_considered: Inline role checks in handlers — no central audit, easy to forget
Single monolithic authorization middleware — cannot attach different policies per route
Decorator metadata only — requires a reader and still needs a guard to enforce

primitives.name: ValueTransform
primitives.purpose: Strongly-typed parse/validate step that converts a raw inbound argument (body/query/param) into the typed value the handler expects.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, TypeVar
from dataclasses import dataclass

I = TypeVar('I')
O = TypeVar('O')

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ArgumentMetadata:
    kind: str
    metatype: type | None
    data: str | None

class ValueTransform(Protocol):
    def transform(self, value: I, meta: ArgumentMetadata) -> O: ...
invariants: transform() MUST raise a typed validation error on bad input; it NEVER returns None to signal invalid.
A ValueTransform MUST be pure: same (value, meta) SHALL produce the same output with no observable side effects.
metatype MUST drive the coercion target; CANNOT silently ignore the declared type.
Composed transforms MUST apply left-to-right in declaration order; swapping order SHALL be explicit.
NEVER mutates the incoming value in place; the returned value is always fresh.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream tools implement ValueTransform (e.g. a ZodValidationPipe-style class) and bind it with a decorator/register call on a parameter or handler; built-in transforms (ParseInt, Validation) MUST satisfy the same Protocol and compose cleanly.

sources.locator: docs.nestjs.com/pipes — transform(value, metadata: ArgumentMetadata) where kind ∈ body|query|param|custom

sources.source: ASP.NET Core 8.0 — Model binding and validation

primitives.why_essential: A handler that receives raw strings has to re-validate the same fields on every path; one contract lets validators/coercers be shared across all entry points and keeps error shapes consistent.
alternatives_considered: Validation inside each handler — duplicated logic, inconsistent errors
Manual parsing with framework helpers only — no composition of custom rules
JSON-Schema only — cannot express cross-field rules cleanly

primitives.name: ConfigBinding
primitives.purpose: Binds a namespaced slice of the runtime configuration to a typed record, validated at startup so misconfiguration fails loud, not silent.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Type, TypeVar

T = TypeVar('T')

class ConfigBinding(Protocol):
    def bind(self, prefix: str, schema: Type[T]) -> T: ...
    def reload(self) -> None: ...
invariants: bind() MUST fail loudly if required keys are missing or typed coercion fails; it NEVER returns a partially-filled record.
Bound records MUST be frozen/immutable; runtime code CANNOT mutate a bound option to affect another consumer.
reload() MUST produce a new record without aliasing the previous one; references already handed out SHALL NOT silently mutate.
Unknown keys under the prefix MUST be reported as errors by default (strict binding) and NEVER silently dropped.
Precedence order (env > file > defaults) MUST be fixed and documented; a later source CANNOT override a value an operator pinned.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream tools declare a dataclass schema and call bind(prefix, schema); alternative sources (YAML file, env, Vault, ConfigMap) plug in as providers via a registered adapter/provider that the binding composes left-to-right.

sources.source: Spring Boot 3.x Reference — Type-safe Configuration Properties

primitives.why_essential: Parsing env vars and dictionary lookups scattered through a codebase is a long tail of production outages; one binder catches errors at startup and gives every tool the same typed window into config.
alternatives_considered: Read os.environ directly — no schema, silent typos
Dict-of-dicts passed around — no validation, no defaults
Per-module singleton loaders — drift in key naming and precedence

primitives.name: HealthProbe
primitives.purpose: Small probe that reports UP/DOWN/DEGRADED with optional detail so orchestrators (Kubernetes, load balancers) can route traffic safely.
primitives.api_signature:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Mapping, Protocol

class HealthStatus(str, Enum):
    UP = 'up'
    DOWN = 'down'
    DEGRADED = 'degraded'

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HealthReport:
    status: HealthStatus
    details: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)

class HealthProbe(Protocol):
    name: str
    async def check(self) -> HealthReport: ...
invariants: check() MUST complete within a declared timeout; a hanging probe SHALL be treated as DOWN.
A probe MUST NEVER throw; unexpected exceptions SHALL be caught and turned into DOWN with the exception class as detail.
name MUST be unique within the registry; duplicate registrations SHALL be rejected.
details MUST NOT leak secrets (connection strings, tokens); callers CANNOT rely on raw credentials appearing.
The aggregated readiness endpoint MUST be UP only when every required probe is UP; optional probes CANNOT force readiness false.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream tools implement HealthProbe and register via a decorator/register() call; the aggregator composes probes into readiness and liveness groups, and new probe sources plug in without changing the endpoint code.
primitives.why_essential: Kubernetes and load balancers make routing decisions from the /health endpoint; if every tool owns its own probe shape, readiness signals conflict and deployments fail to roll back safely.
alternatives_considered: Single monolithic /health handler — every team edits the same file
TCP port open as readiness — ignores app-level failures
Per-service custom /ping formats — blocks generic orchestrator checks

primitives.name: LifecycleHook
primitives.purpose: Named callback fired at a defined application phase (starting, ready, stopping) so tools can initialize resources and shut down cleanly.
primitives.api_signature:
from enum import Enum
from typing import Awaitable, Callable

class LifecyclePhase(str, Enum):
    STARTING = 'starting'
    READY = 'ready'
    STOPPING = 'stopping'
    STOPPED = 'stopped'

LifecycleCallback = Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]

class LifecycleHook:
    def __init__(self, phase: LifecyclePhase, cb: LifecycleCallback) -> None:
        self.phase = phase
        self.cb = cb
invariants: READY MUST fire exactly once, after STARTING and all startup callbacks have completed successfully.
STOPPING hooks MUST run in reverse registration order (LIFO) so later-initialized resources drain first.
A failing STARTING hook MUST prevent READY from firing; the app SHALL transition to STOPPED with non-zero exit.
Hooks MUST NOT block indefinitely; each hook SHALL obey a configured timeout and be cancelled otherwise.
No hook CAN re-enter its own phase; recursive registration of the same callback in the same phase SHALL raise.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream tools instantiate LifecycleHook and register via a decorator/register()/@Observes-style binder on the application's lifecycle registry; alternative sources (Spring ApplicationReadyEvent, Quarkus StartupEvent, ASP.NET IHostApplicationLifetime) plug in through adapters that map native events onto LifecyclePhase.
primitives.consumption_example:
async def warm_cache() -> None:
    return None

hook = LifecycleHook(LifecyclePhase.READY, warm_cache)
assert hook.phase == LifecyclePhase.READY

sources.source: Spring Boot 3.x Reference — Application Events and Listeners

primitives.why_essential: Graceful startup and shutdown sequencing (warm caches, drain connections, flush buffers) CANNOT be invented per tool; a shared hook vocabulary lets orchestrators trust the app's readiness and shutdown signals.
alternatives_considered: atexit-style hooks only — no STARTING phase, no async support
Per-tool startup scripts — ordering is ad-hoc, failures invisible
Single giant startup function — monolithic, blocks parallel init

primitives.name: FeatureToggle
primitives.purpose: Named boolean (or variant) predicate, evaluated against the current context, that controls whether a code path is live for a given request.
invariants: is_active() MUST be pure given the same (key, ctx); side effects (I/O, random draws) SHALL NEVER leak into evaluation.
Evaluation MUST default to False (off) when the backing store is unreachable; CANNOT default to on.
A toggle key MUST be unique within the registry and SHALL follow a fixed naming convention.
The evaluation path MUST record an observability event (toggle key + decision) for every call; audit entries NEVER are dropped.
Removing a toggle MUST be a two-step deprecation: mark stale, then delete; code references CANNOT disappear abruptly.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream tools declare a FeatureToggle (e.g. an enum member or a class), register a strategy/provider (percent-rollout, per-tenant, per-role), and evaluation runs through the configured provider so new stores (Togglz/Spring @ConditionalOnProperty/OpenFeature) plug in as adapters.
primitives.why_essential: Feature flags straddle code, product, and ops; without one contract, each tool reinvents on-off logic, audits drift, and there is no single place to list what is live in prod.
alternatives_considered: If-statements on env vars — no per-user rollout, no audit
Runtime config reloads only — no context-aware evaluation
Manual DNS/Traffic splits — wrong layer; operates on infrastructure not logic

primitives.name: RouterPipeline
primitives.purpose: Named bundle of middleware (e.g. 'browser', 'api') that a route joins with pipe_through so groups of endpoints share the same pre-dispatch chain.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Sequence

class RouterPipeline(Protocol):
    name: str
    middleware: Sequence['Middleware']

    def attach(self, route: str) -> None: ...
invariants: A pipeline MUST run its middleware in declared order, every time; reorder at runtime SHALL NEVER happen.
A route joined to a pipeline MUST execute its chain before the handler; the chain CANNOT be bypassed per request.
Pipelines MUST NOT share mutable state across requests; any state SHALL live in RequestContext.assigns.
Joining a route to a pipeline MUST be declarative; programmatic attach CANNOT happen after the router is sealed.
A pipeline name MUST be unique within the router; duplicate declarations SHALL raise at boot.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream tools declare a pipeline via a register() call or a pipeline/2-style macro, then scoped routes join it with a pipe_through directive; frameworks like Phoenix or Rails Rack chains plug in by providing their own adapter that respects the name and order invariants.
primitives.consumption_example:
def build_api(router: dict) -> None:
    p: RouterPipeline = router['pipelines']['api']
    p.attach('/v1/users/:id')

# At compile time, pipeline ensures order:
assert hasattr(RouterPipeline, 'attach')
primitives.why_essential: Route groups share concerns (auth, parsing, throttling); without one vocabulary, 'add auth to /api' becomes a per-file change and regressions appear when a route is added outside the group.
alternatives_considered: Per-route decorator stacks — duplication across many handlers
Single global middleware chain — cannot vary by route group
URL-prefix-based conditionals in middleware — fragile, easy to miss

primitives.name: EventBus
primitives.purpose: In-process publish/subscribe point for named framework and application events (e.g. sql.active_record, http.request) with structured payloads.
primitives.api_signature:
from typing import Any, Callable, Mapping, Protocol

Subscriber = Callable[[str, Mapping[str, Any]], None]

class EventBus(Protocol):
    def publish(self, name: str, payload: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None: ...
    def subscribe(self, pattern: str, handler: Subscriber) -> Callable[[], None]: ...
invariants: publish() MUST deliver to every matching subscriber synchronously OR through a declared executor; delivery order per subscriber SHALL be the subscription order.
A subscriber that raises MUST NOT abort delivery to other subscribers; the error SHALL be reported to the observability sink.
The returned unsubscribe callable MUST be idempotent; calling it twice CANNOT remove a different subscription.
Event names MUST follow a dotted namespace (e.g. 'sql.active_record'); wildcards SHALL use a documented pattern syntax.
Payloads MUST be treated as immutable by subscribers; mutating a payload to signal another subscriber is FORBIDDEN.
primitives.extension_contract: Downstream tools publish named events via publish() and consumers subscribe via subscribe()/an @EventListener-style decorator; tracing/metrics plug in as a provider that subscribes to patterns (e.g. '*.active_record') without touching producers.
primitives.consumption_example:
def on_sql(name: str, payload: dict) -> None:
    duration = payload.get('duration', 0)
    _ = (name, duration)

bus: EventBus
unsub = bus.subscribe('sql.*', on_sql)
bus.publish('sql.query', {'duration': 12})
unsub()
primitives.why_essential: Observability code (tracing, audit, metrics) MUST attach to framework internals without forking the framework; a bus turns 'I need to know when X happens' into a subscription instead of a patch.
alternatives_considered: AOP/monkey-patching around framework methods — fragile and invisible
Dedicated callbacks per concern — combinatorial wiring
External broker for in-process events — overkill latency and ops burden

cross_cutting_insights: All six frameworks converge on three lifetimes (process, request, per-call); the naming differs (Spring 'request' vs ASP.NET 'Scoped' vs Nest.js 'REQUEST') but the semantics are identical and portable.

Every framework exposes a per-request state carrier (HttpContext, Plug.Conn, CurrentAttributes, ExecutionContext) — identity, correlation id, and tenant are ALWAYS attached here, never via thread-local globals.

Configuration binding is a startup concern (Spring @ConfigurationProperties, ASP.NET IOptions<T>): validation happens once, results are immutable, and unknown keys fail fast rather than at first read.
Middleware/Plug/Interceptor chains are all the same pattern under different names: ordered (ctx, call_next) callables with short-circuit via halt()/non-call, making ordering a first-class contract.

Lifecycle hooks have stabilized into STARTING/READY/STOPPING phases (Spring ApplicationReadyEvent, Quarkus StartupEvent/ShutdownEvent, ASP.NET IHostApplicationLifetime); orchestrators rely on the READY signal to gate traffic.
Health endpoints are composite: a registry of named probes aggregated by a StatusAggregator (Spring) or equivalent; readiness != liveness and the two MUST be reported separately.
Guard-vs-Pipe-vs-Interceptor ordering (Nest.js) encodes a production truth: authorize before transforming, transform before handling, observe around all of them.
Feature flags and Spring @ConditionalOnProperty / @Profile share one mental model: a named predicate evaluated against context controls whether a wiring or code path is live.
gaps_observed: SKILL-001 lacks a LifetimeScope enum; lifetimes are currently implicit in tool bodies rather than declared at registration.
CorrelationId propagation across outbound HTTP/queue calls is not a declared primitive; each integration tool handles headers its own way.
No unified HealthProbe registry aggregating /readyz and /livez across tools; each generator adds its own path with its own shape.
LifecycleHook phases (STARTING/READY/STOPPING) are not a first-class primitive; startup wiring is scattered across generators.
FeatureToggle as a context-aware predicate is absent; the current flag story is environment-variable checks without per-tenant evaluation.
